mainTopic: Whether a קונם prohibition stays on an item after it is given as a gift, and whether the laws of מעילה apply to קונמות
overview: The גמרא challenges רבא with a ברייתא about a man who refused to lend his cow or spade and made a vow. The ברייתא says the item becomes permitted once the vower dies or once it is given as a gift. רב אחא בריה דרב איקא answers that the gift came through a third person, not from the vower himself. רב אשי supports this from the ברייתא's wording: 'it was given,' not 'he gave.' Then a new topic opens. רבא asks רב נחמן whether the laws of מעילה (misusing הקדש) apply to items forbidden by a קונם. רב נחמן proves from a משנה that a קונם is like הקדש, so there is מעילה. The גמרא shows this is a dispute: רבי מאיר holds there is מעילה in קונמות, and the חכמים hold there is not. Finally, רב אשי rules that when someone gives a forbidden loaf as a gift, the receiver commits מעילה once he uses it.

steps.title: A teaching about a refused cow and spade challenges רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: a man refuses to lend his cow or spade and makes a קונם. The item is forbidden while the vower is alive, but permitted if he dies or if it was given as a gift. This seems to contradict רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: Someone said, 'Lend me your cow.' The owner said, 'Any cow I bought is קונם for you,' or 'My property is forbidden to you if I have any cow except this one.' Someone said, 'Lend me your spade.' The owner said, 'Any spade I bought is קונם,' or 'My property is forbidden to me if I have any spade except this one.' It turns out he does have another one. While he is alive, it is forbidden. If he died, or if it was given to the other person as a gift, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to attack רבא's earlier ruling. The ברייתא says that if the item was given to the other person as a gift, it becomes permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא held that the item stays forbidden to the other person even after the vower gives it to him as a gift. The ברייתא says plainly that a gift makes it permitted. So the ברייתא seems to argue with רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Lend me
A vow word that makes something forbidden like a קרבן
A spade or axe
My property is forbidden to you
During his lifetime it is forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: The vow here works because the owner was lying: he said he had no other cow or spade, but he really did. Because of that, the vow takes effect. In the 'קונם' wording, his other cows or spades become forbidden. In the 'if I have' wording, the condition is fulfilled, so his property becomes forbidden.

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him: If someone said to him: 'Lend me your cow,'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: ״קֻוֽנָּם פָּרָה שֶׁאֲנִי קָנוּי לָךְ״,
phrases.english: and he answered him: 'Any cow that I bought is קונם for you,'

phrases.aramaic: ״נְכָסַי עָלֶיךָ אִם יֵשׁ לִי פָּרָה אֶלָּא זוֹ״.
phrases.english: or 'My property is forbidden to you if I have a cow other than this one.'
Or someone said: 'Lend me your spade,' and he answered him:
'Any spade that I have, that I bought, is קונם,'

phrases.aramaic: ״נְכָסַי עָלַי אִם יֵשׁ לִי קַרְדּוֹם אֶלָּא זֶה״,
phrases.english: or 'My property is forbidden to me if I have a spade other than this one,'
and it turns out that he does have one,
then during his lifetime it is forbidden;
if he died, or if it was given to him as a gift,
it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's ruling from the previous discussion
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that an item forbidden by a קונם stays forbidden even after the vower gives it as a gift
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says a gift makes the item permitted, which seems to contradict רבא

steps.title: The gift came through a third person
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא explains that the ברייתא means the item reached the other person through someone else, not straight from the vower.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רב איקא said: It means it was given to him by another person.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא defends רבא by reading the ברייתא as talking about a gift that came through a third person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the vower first gave the item to someone else, it left his ownership, and then that third person gave it as a gift. In that case it is permitted. When the vower himself gives it, it stays forbidden, just as רבא said.

keyTerms.meaning: Through another person
That it was given to him

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rav Ika, said:
It means that it was given to him by another person.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to mean any gift, even from the vower himself
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only means a gift that came through a third person, so רבא's ruling stands

steps.title: The exact wording supports the answer
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי points out that the ברייתא says 'it was given to him' and not 'he gave it to him,' which fits the idea that a third person gave it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The wording also shows this, because it says 'that it was given to him,' and not 'that he gave it to him.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings support for the previous answer from the exact words of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the vower himself were the giver, the ברייתא would say 'he gave it to him.' Instead it uses a passive form, 'it was given,' which hints that someone else gave it. This backs up רב אחא's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also precise (supports this)
It teaches / it says
That he gave it to him

steps.whatToRemember: An item forbidden by a קונם stays forbidden if the vower himself hands it over as a gift. It becomes permitted only if it reaches the other person through someone else.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: The wording is also precise,
because it teaches: 'that it was given to him,'
and it does not teach: 'that he gave it to him.'

steps.raayaObject: רב אחא's reading that the gift came through a third person
steps.raayaSupportSource: The passive wording 'שֶׁנִּיתְּנָה לוֹ' in the ברייתא

steps.title: Does מעילה apply to items forbidden by a קונם
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן whether someone who uses an item forbidden by a קונם is guilty of מעילה, like someone who misuses הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked רב נחמן: Is there מעילה with קונמות, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. רבא asks whether the laws of misusing הקדש apply to items forbidden by a קונם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קונם makes an item forbidden 'like a קרבן.' The question is whether that comparison is complete, so that misusing it brings the laws of מעילה. Or does the comparison only make the item forbidden?

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him
Misusing הקדש, which brings a קרבן and a payment
Items forbidden by a קונם vow
Or not?

steps.whyThisMatters: This question tests how far the comparison between a קונם and הקדש really goes.

phrases.english: Rava asked Rav Nachman:
Is there מעילה with things forbidden by a קונם, or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the previous discussion ends
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the laws of מעילה apply to items forbidden by a קונם

steps.title: רב נחמן: A קונם is like הקדש, so there is מעילה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers רבא from an earlier משנה. It says that payment taken for returning a lost item 'falls to הקדש,' which shows that a קונם is treated like הקדש and carries מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You already learned it in a משנה. 'In a place where people take payment for returning a lost item, that benefit should go to הקדש.' This means a קונם is like הקדש. Just as הקדש has מעילה, so too קונמות have מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבא's question from step 4. He brings a משנה showing that something forbidden by a קונם is treated like הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that any payment from a forbidden benefit 'should fall to הקדש.' רב נחמן reads that wording as saying that a קונם actually has the status of הקדש. If it is really like הקדש, then the rules of מעילה should apply to it too.

keyTerms.meaning: The sin of using הקדש for ordinary, personal purposes
Property that belongs to the בית המקדש
Vows that make an item forbidden, said using the word 'קונם'
Payment or wages

phrases.english: He said to him: You learned it:
phrases.notes: רב נחמן is answering רבא, pointing him to a משנה on 33a.

phrases.english: In a place where people take payment for it
the benefit should fall to הקדש.
That is to say, it is like הקדש;
just as הקדש has מעילה,
so too קונמות have מעילה.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, there is מעילה in קונמות, because a משנה treats a קונם like הקדש.

steps.title: A dispute of תנאים: רבי מאיר's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that this question is a dispute between תנאים. רבי מאיר says that saying 'this loaf is הקדש' brings מעילה for everyone, while saying 'this loaf is upon me as הקדש' brings מעילה only for the person who made the vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute of תנאים. If someone said, 'This loaf is קונם, הקדש,' and then it was eaten, whether he ate it or his friend ate it, the eater committed מעילה. Therefore the loaf can be redeemed. If someone said, 'This loaf is upon me as הקדש,' and he ate it, he committed מעילה, but his friend did not. Therefore it cannot be redeemed. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says that רב נחמן's answer matches one side of an older dispute between תנאים. It starts by quoting רבי מאיר's view, and the next step gives the opposing view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that there is מעילה in קונמות. He divides between two kinds of wording. 'This loaf is הקדש' gives the loaf itself a holy status, so anyone who eats it commits מעילה and it can be redeemed. 'Upon me' only forbids it to the speaker, so only he commits מעילה, and there is no פדיון.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Like the תנאים.' The question matches an older dispute between תנאים
Redeeming an item to remove its holy status
'Upon me.' The item is forbidden only to the speaker

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. In the first, the loaf itself becomes הקדש for everyone. In the second, it is forbidden only to the person who vowed.

phrases.english: It is like a dispute of תנאים:
'This loaf is קונם, הקדש,' and it was eaten,
whether he or his friend ate it, he committed מעילה;
therefore it can be redeemed.
'This loaf is upon me as הקדש,' and it was eaten:
if he ate it, he committed מעילה; if his friend did, he did not.
Therefore it cannot be redeemed.
These are the words of רבי מאיר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Places רב נחמן's answer within an older dispute between תנאים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: there is מעילה in קונמות. Whether everyone or only the vower is liable depends on the wording of the vow.

steps.title: The חכמים: no מעילה in קונמות
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים disagree with רבי מאיר. In both cases nobody commits מעילה, because קונמות do not carry מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: in either case there is no מעילה, because there is no מעילה in קונמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side of the dispute. The חכמים hold that a קונם never brings מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, a קונם makes an item forbidden, but it is not true הקדש. So the rules of מעילה do not apply. רב נחמן's answer therefore fits רבי מאיר and not the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: The majority of Sages who disagree with רבי מאיר
'Either way.' This covers both kinds of wording

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר holds there is מעילה in קונמות. The חכמים hold there is no מעילה in קונמות.

phrases.english: And the חכמים say:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ לֹא מָעַל,
phrases.english: in either case, he did not commit מעילה,
because there is no מעילה in קונמות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposing side of the dispute begun in step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no מעילה in קונמות at all.

steps.title: Who is guilty of מעילה when a forbidden loaf is given as a gift?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב אויא asks רב אשי about a case where someone says 'my loaf is forbidden to you' and then gives it to him as a gift. It seems that neither person can be guilty of מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בריה דרב אויא said to רב אשי: If someone says 'My loaf is forbidden to you,' and then gives it to him as a gift, who committed מעילה? Should the giver be guilty? But the loaf is not forbidden to him! Should the receiver be guilty? He can say, 'I wanted something permitted. I did not want something forbidden.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. It assumes there is מעילה in קונמות and asks which person, the giver or the receiver, is the one who commits it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The giver cannot be guilty, since the loaf was never forbidden to him. The receiver also seems free of guilt, because he can claim he only meant to accept a permitted gift. So the question is whether anyone at all is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: The giver
The receiver
A gift
'I wanted something permitted'

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַוְיָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: רב אחא son of רב אויא said to רב אשי:
'My loaf is forbidden to you,'
and he gave it to him as a gift: who committed מעילה?
Should the giver be guilty of מעילה?
But it is not forbidden to him!
Should the receiver be guilty of מעילה?
He can say:
'I wanted something permitted; I did not want something forbidden.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַוְיָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the view that there is מעילה in קונמות and asks how it works in a gift case
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In a gift case, which person is guilty of מעילה: the giver or the receiver?

steps.title: רב אשי: The receiver is guilty once he uses it
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the receiver commits מעילה when he uses the loaf. מעילה normally happens when someone uses הקדש by mistake, thinking it is ordinary.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The receiver commits מעילה once he uses it. Anyone who uses הקדש money for ordinary purposes, thinking it is ordinary, commits מעילה. This person also commits מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question: the receiver is the guilty one. His claim 'I didn't want something forbidden' does not help him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual case of מעילה is someone who uses הקדש without knowing it is holy. So the receiver's lack of intent to use something forbidden is exactly the normal case of מעילה, and it does not excuse him. He becomes guilty at the moment he actually uses the loaf.

keyTerms.meaning: When he uses it up or spends it
Ordinary, non-holy things
Thinking, mistakenly believing

steps.whatToRemember: In the gift case, the receiver commits מעילה when he uses the loaf, even though he did not know it was forbidden. מעילה is normally done by mistake anyway.

phrases.english: He said to him:
The receiver commits מעילה when he uses it,
for anyone who uses הקדש money for ordinary purposes,
thinking it is ordinary, commits מעילה.
This one too commits מעילה.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The receiver is guilty of מעילה when he uses the loaf, because מעילה is normally committed by someone who thinks the item is ordinary.
